title: Admin audit provenance trail and sealed storage orchestration
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers require a tamper-evident, region-aware audit record for all admin actions, access events, and configuration changes. Current audit exports lack a single canonical provenance trail combining per-region WORM storage, signed integrity checkpoints, and automated evidence bundles for compliance attestations.

Goal: Build an orchestration layer and storage pattern that: (1) captures admin actions, access grants/revocations, and config changes with structured metadata; (2) persists canonical audit bundles to WORM-backed stores in the customer-designated residency region; (3) produces cryptographic checkpoints (Merkle roots + signature) and periodic attestation reports; and (4) exposes automated evidence export endpoints for auditors (S3-compatible export + signed manifest).
implementation_notes: Event capture: extend existing audit pipeline to include structured 'provenance' fields: actor_id, actor_role, action_type, resource_path, before/after config blob (diff-friendly), request_id, region_tag, and retention_policy_id.

Canonical bundle: group events into time-windowed bundles (configurable window 1m-1h) and canonicalize ordering deterministically by (timestamp, request_id). Each bundle gets a bundle_id and an accompanying JSON manifest describing contained events and retention/residency metadata.

WORM storage strategy: integrate with immutable object backends (customer WORM S3, cloud object lock, or internal sealed-store). Orchestration will write primary bundle plus a small index file and a signed checkpoint file (Merkle root of bundle) to the region-designated WORM endpoint.

Signing and attestations: runtime service will sign the checkpoint with a platform KMS key; for Private deployments support customer HSM/KMS signing. Store signatures alongside bundle metadata and publish a periodic attestation ledger (daily) with checkpoint references.

Evidence export: provide an API to request an evidence package for a time range and region. The package includes bundles, manifests, signature proofs, and an export manifest (SHA256 checksums). Exports are available as downloadable archive or pushed to customer export sink (S3/GCS) with retention metadata.

Integrity monitoring: implement periodic re-hash job that re-calculates Merkle roots from read-only WORM storage and alerts if any mismatch occurs. Maintain an 'integrity timeline' in the console for audit review.

Retention policy enforcement: tie bundles to retention_policy_id; lifecycle workers will ensure bundles are retained or expired according to policy and regional laws. Deletion operations must produce a 'deletion-proof' event recorded as a bundle before expiry window begins.
Backfill and migration: provide tooling to backfill historic audit events into the canonical bundle format and sign retroactively where possible; record any gaps and surface to customers.

Operational considerations: account for high-throughput customers by supporting batching thresholds and asynchronous persisted manifests; ensure write retry semantics with idempotence using bundle_id and request_id dedupe.
Compatibility: ensure bundles are compatible with existing console evidence viewer and the audit-export CLI; include parsers in SDKs for downstream verifier tooling.
alternatives_considered: Option A: Append-only DB with snapshots + export. Rejected because DB snapshots are not accepted by some auditors as immutable WORM and cross-region residency mapping is complex.
Option B: Per-event signatures instead of bundle Merkle roots. Rejected due to high operational overhead and larger metadata blowup at scale.

Option C: Rely solely on cloud provider object-lock features. Kept as a supported backend but not as the only enforcement mechanism because not every deployment (on-prem/private) will accept provider-managed locks.
acceptance_criteria: All admin actions, access events, and config changes are captured in the new canonical bundle schema for 95% of production traffic in a canary region.
Bundles are written to a WORM-backed store in the configured residency region within the configured window, with a signed checkpoint file persisted alongside each bundle.
API to request an evidence package returns a signed archive with bundle manifests and checksums; automated export to S3 test bucket succeeds end-to-end in QA.
Integrity rehash job detects no mismatches for canary bundles; simulated tamper detection test results in alert and a documented incident runbook trigger.
Console shows an integrity timeline and bundle-level metadata (region, retention policy, signature status) in the audit evidence view.
Retention lifecycle jobs honor retention_policy_id and record deletion-intent events prior to final expiry for auditability.
Security review sign-off obtained, and HSM/KMS integration documented for Private deployments.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary - 2 weeks): Implement capture pipeline and bundle writer; run in canary region for low-traffic customers with platform signing.
Phase 2 (QA - 4 weeks): Add WORM backend integrations (S3 Object Lock, sealed-store), implement signer rotation and attestations, QA integrity rehash jobs, and test evidence export flow.
Phase 3 (Gradual rollout - 6 weeks): Enable for larger customers with opt-in; provide migration tooling for backfills and console visibility.

Phase 4 (GA): Default bundle capture for all hosted accounts, enable customer-configured residency mapping and retention policies; offer enterprise onboarding for Private deployments with HSM signing.
monitoring_and_alerting: Metric: checkpoint_signing_latency (p95 <= 500ms on platform KMS; configurable for HSM)
Metric: integrity_mismatch_count (should be 0; trigger P0 pager if >0)
Alert: export_failure when evidence export job fails repeatedly (>3 retries)
Alert: retention_policy_violation when a bundle scheduled for deletion is missing deletion-proof event
